title: Redwood Feb 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly all-hands focused on Q1 priorities: ramping Dedicated capacity, Private deployments roadmap, reliability/latency improvements, SOC 2 compliance update, hiring plan, and a short product demo of the new Console observability features. Leadership fielded questions on pricing, Dedicated availability, and EU region rollouts.
next_steps: Leadership to send slides and deck link after call
Product to publish Console demo recording and release notes
Infra to share Dedicated capacity timelines with Sales
People Ops to post updated hiring plan and referral bonuses

Sofia Martinez - record and upload Console demo clip - 2026-03-02
Maya Singh - share post-mortem and latency dashboard link - 2026-03-03
Ellen Park - circulate Q1 hiring plan and interview rubric - 2026-03-05
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-28
Start: 10:00 PST (recording started)
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (CEO); Maya Singh (CTO); Liam O'Connor (VP Eng); Sofia Martinez (Head of Product); Ellen Park (Head of People); and ~120 others (all-hands).

Summary: Jordan opens w/ quick wins, Maya covers infra and SOC 2, Sofia demos Console updates, Q&A closes.

[00:00] Jordan Reyes: Hey, good morning everyone, uh thanks for joining. Quick agenda, I'll do a 10 minute update on company metrics, Maya will cover infra and reliability, Sofia has a quick demo of Console, and then we'll do Q&A.

[00:25] Jordan Reyes: Q1 things, we're seeing steady adoption in Hosted and Dedicated. Monthly active API keys up about 18% month over month — that helps our ARR motion, um revenue tracking is on plan for the quarter. We're still, uh, watching unit economics, cost per token is down a touch thanks to batching improvements.

[00:50] Jordan Reyes: Big shout-out to the teams that shipped the new routing policies and the prefix cache changes. I know the infra folks slogged through some messy kernel issues, so thanks.

[01:20] Maya Singh: Hi everyone. Quick infra update — SOC 2 was completed last week, final paperwork in the drive, we'll post the cert and a short FAQ. On latency, we pushed a few kernel and memory tweaks, sequences under 1k tokens now 12% lower p95 across our standard model catalog. There's still some outliers when we route to older quantized variants, we're looking into better heuristic for fallback.

[01:55] Maya Singh: Also, EU region — we've got the control plane and initial Dedicated pools up in eu-central. Not full capacity yet, but Sales can start talking to customers about region availability this month. We still have a couple of networking bits to clean up for Private deployments in EMEA.

[02:30] Liam O'Connor: On Dedicated, we've made real progress on autoscaling — the new burst capacity policy reduces cold start tail latencies; early internal benchmarks show 25% fewer timeouts during spikes. We do need to communicate expected throughput per unit better to customers, so we're drafting a 'throughput guide' for each GPU type.

[03:05] Sofia Martinez: Product update — Console now has token-level cost breakdowns in the route view and an improved trace UI. Demo link will be posted. New rollouts feature supports canary and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when quality thresholds pass. We still need to clean up naming in the UI, some labels say "KV cash" in the telemetry view (laughs) — obviously should be KV cache, we'll fix that.

[03:40] Sofia Martinez: Quick demo: open console, select model route, you can see latency heatmap, cost per route, and then drill into a single request trace. We also added a prompt evaluation panel to compare outputs across model variants — it's handy for regressions.

[04:30] Jordan Reyes: On go-to-market — self-serve is doing well, but there's a consistent pattern of mid-market deals requiring Dedicated or Private within the 2–6 month window. So we need tighter sales <> infra alignment to avoid overpromising.

[05:05] Jordan Reyes: We're also starting a small program for reference customers who want to run benchmarks. It'll be limited to a handful of partners and we'll provide a benchmark kit + support from SEs.

[05:30] Audience question (attendee via chat): When will Dedicated be generally available?

[05:40] Liam O'Connor: Short answer: we're moving to GA in waves. Some GPU types GA next quarter, others later — we'll share the exact timeline with Sales by Friday. The big constraint has been scheduling and some memory config issues on older cards.

[06:10] Audience question: Can we expect price changes if customers use fallback to cheaper variants?

[06:20] Sofia Martinez: Pricing will be per model variant and per route; fallback is policy-driven and customers will see cost telemetry. We'll produce a pricing explainer doc, because yes, it can change per request if the fallback uses a different model.

[06:50] Maya Singh: Security/compliance note — SOC 2 covers our hosted control plane and storage. Private deployments have a different audit surface; we now have a checklist for customers and partners to complete for on-prem installations.

[07:15] Audience: Are we targeting any specific compliance for EU customers?

[07:24] Maya Singh: Right now SOC 2 is baseline, for EU customers data residency is top ask; we have EU control plane and we're talking through local KMS integrations — expect more on that in the next update.

[07:50] Jordan Reyes: Hiring update from Ellen.

[07:55] Ellen Park: Quick hiring summary — Q1 we are prioritizing senior infra engineers, SE headcount for EMEA, and two product managers focused on Console and Optimize. We're also adjusting interview rubrics to emphasize production serving experience. We'll post the full plan and referral bonuses later today.

[08:15] Ellen Park: Reminder: new parental leave changes go into effect March 15. People Ops will send details in Slack.

[08:30] Jordan Reyes: A quick finance note — burn rate is consistent with plan; we made a small revision on reserved capacity pricing assumptions but no near-term headcount freezes. Good.

[08:50] Audience question: Any updates on competitors or market moves?

[08:58] Jordan Reyes: We've seen continued noise from the big cloud vendors — bedrock updates, Anthropic's new model announcements, etc. Our advantage remains production economics and predictable latency. Keep monitoring but don't panic.

[09:20] Sofia Martinez: One more product note — Optimize now recommends quantization profiles based on workload; early results show up to 35% cost savings for some customers with minor output delta. Ops is running A/B tests.

[09:50] Audience: Will we open-source any eval tooling?

[09:56] Maya Singh: We plan to publish a lightweight eval harness and reference prompt sets later this quarter; it's part of our community strategy.

[10:15] Jordan Reyes: Ok we'll do a quick lightning Q&A. Please keep questions concise.

[10:25] Audience question (Engineering): Is there a known blocker on KV cache scaling?

[10:30] Liam O'Connor: Yes, a couple of consistency issues when scaling the cache across multi-tenant hosts; we have a patch in test, hoping to roll next week.

[10:45] Audience (Sales): Do we have new security docs for procurement?

[10:50] Maya Singh: Yes, security pack is in the drive, includes SOC 2 report and an FAQ. We'll add a procurement checklist too.

[11:05] Jordan Reyes: Closing remarks — focus on hitting GA milestones, keep cadence on reliability tickets, and be proactive with Sales about Dedicated timelines. Thanks for the work, big month ahead.

[11:25] Jordan Reyes: We'll follow up with slides and recording. End of meeting.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional ASR errors and shorthand; some proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., KV cash). Links referenced: slides: drive.redwood/company/all-hands/feb-2026 (internal), console-demo: drive.redwood/product/console/demo-clip-2026-02-28.mp4, security pack: drive.redwood/security/soc2-2026.pdf
